chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Al-imlak occurs and is scattered upon the people,' so he said: 'It is forbidden, but eat what they give you from it.'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq.
key_terms.الْإِمْلاَكُ: A specific type of food or gift distributed among people, often associated with weddings or social gatherings.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on consuming gifts or food distributed as 'imlak' in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the ritual act of distributing *al-imlak* (often identified as a specific type of bread or cake) and the permissibility of consuming it, ruling the distribution itself as *haram* while allowing individuals to eat what is given to them. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of separating the prohibition of a specific ceremonial practice from the general permissibility of the item, ensuring that believers are not deprived of sustenance due to the ritual's invalidity. The hadith highlights the nuanced approach of the Imams in preserving communal customs while correcting their religious status.
